'''Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel''' ({{IPA|de|ˈbɛsl̩|lang}}; 22 July 1784 – 17 March 1846) was a German [[astronomer]], [[mathematician]], [[physicist]], and [[geodesy|geodesist]]. He was the first astronomer who determined reliable values for the distance from the Sun to another star by the method of [[parallax]]. Certain important mathematical functions were first studied systematically by Bessel and were named [[Bessel function]]s in his honour.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Dutka |first1=Jacques |title=On the early history of Bessel functions |journal=Archive for History of Exact Sciences |date=1995 |volume=49 |issue=2 |pages=105–134 |doi=10.1007/BF00376544}}</ref>

== Life and family ==
Bessel was born in [[Minden]], [[Westphalia]], then capital of the Prussian administrative region [[Minden-Ravensberg]], as second son of a civil servant into a large family. At the age of 14 he left the school, because he did not like the education in Latin language, and apprenticed in the import-export concern Kulenkamp at [[Bremen]]. The business's reliance on cargo ships led him to turn his [[mathematics|mathematical]] skills to problems in [[navigation]]. This in turn led to an interest in [[astronomy]] as a way of determining [[longitude]].

Bessel came to the attention of [[Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers]], a practising physician of Bremen and well-known astronomer, by producing a refinement on the orbital calculations for [[Halley's Comet]] in 1804, using old observation data taken from [[Thomas Harriot]] and [[Nathaniel Torporley]] in 1607.{{sfn|Chisholm|1911}} [[Franz Xaver von Zach]] edited the results in his journal ''Monatliche Correspondenz''.

Having finished his commercial education, Bessel left Kulenkamp in 1806 and became assistant at [[Johann Hieronymus Schröter]]'s private observatory in [[Lilienthal, Lower Saxony|Lilienthal]] near Bremen as successor of [[Karl Ludwig Harding]]. There he worked on [[James Bradley]]'s stellar observation data to produce precise positions for some 3,222 stars.{{sfn|Chisholm|1911}}

Despite lacking any higher education, especially at university, Bessel was appointed director of the newly founded [[Königsberg Observatory]] by King [[Frederick William III of Prussia]] in January 1810, at the age of 25, and remained in that position until his death. Some elder professors of the Philosophical Faculty disputed Bessel's right to teach mathematics without any academic degree. Therefore, he turned to his fellow [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]], who provided the award of an honorary doctor degree from the [[University of Göttingen]] in March 1811. Both scientists were in correspondence from 1804 to 1843. In 1837 they got in quarrel about Gauss's habit of very slow publication.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Biermann | first1 = Kurt-R. | title = Über die Beziehungen zwischen C.F. Gauß und F.W. Bessel | journal = Mitteilungen der Gauss-Gesellschaft Göttingen | volume = 3 | pages = 7–20 | year = 1966 }}</ref>

In 1842 Bessel took part in the annual meeting of the [[British Association for the Advancement of Science]] in Manchester, accompanied by the geophysicist [[Georg Adolf Erman]] and the mathematician [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi]], where he gave a report on astronomical clocks.<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/46628#page/273/mode/1up Report of the British Assiociation for the Advancement of Science.]</ref>

Bessel married Johanna Hagen, the daughter of the chemist and pharmacist [[Karl Gottfried Hagen]] who was the uncle of the physician and biologist [[Hermann August Hagen]] and the hydraulic engineer [[Gotthilf Hagen]], the latter also Bessel's student and assistant from 1816 to 1818. The physicist [[Franz Ernst Neumann]], Bessel's close companion and colleague, was married to Johanna Hagen's sister Florentine. Neumann introduced Bessel's exacting methods of measurement and data reduction into his mathematico-physical seminar, which he co-directed with [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi]] at Königsberg.<ref>{{Cite book | first1=Kathryn M. | last1=Olesko|author1-link= Kathryn Olesko | title=Physics as a Calling: Discipline and Practice in the Königsberg Seminar for Physics | url=https://archive.org/details/physicsascalling00oles | url-access=registration | publisher=Cornell University Press | year=1991 | isbn=978-0-8014-2248-5}}</ref> These exacting methods had a lasting impact upon the work of Neumann's students and upon the Prussian conception of precision in measurement.

Bessel had two sons and three daughters. His elder son became an architect but died suddenly in 1840 aged 26; his younger son died shortly after birth. His eldest daughter, Marie, married the physicist [[Georg Adolf Erman]], member of the scholar family [[Erman]]. One of their sons in turn was the renowned [[Egyptologist]] [[Adolf Erman]]. His third daughter Johanna married the politician [[Adolf Hermann Hagen]]; one of their sons was the physicist [[Ernst Bessel Hagen]], and the mathematician [[Erich Bessel-Hagen]] was their grandson. Bessel was [[Godparent|godfather]] of [[Adolf von Baeyer]], son of his collaborator [[Johann Jacob Baeyer]].

After several months of illness Bessel died in March 1846 at his observatory from [[retroperitoneal fibrosis]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1002/asna.18460240402 | title = Bessel's Tod | language = de| trans-title = Bessel's death| journal = Astronomische Nachrichten | volume = 24 | issue = 556| pages = 49–52 | year = 1846 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=-qAEAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA50| bibcode = 1846AN.....24...49B| last1 = Bessel | first1 = Friedrich Wilhelm }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1007/s001310050044 | last = Neumann-Redlin von Meding | first = E. | title = Vor 150 Jahren: die Beschreibung der Retroperitonealfibrose, der "Ormond'schen Erkrankung", am Krankheitsbild F.W. Bessels (1784–1846) | journal = Der Urologe B | volume = 36| pages = 378–382| year = 1996| issue = 5 }}</ref>

== Work ==
[[File:Koenigsberg observatory.jpg|right|thumb|[[Königsberg Observatory]] (1830)]]
[[File:Friedrich.Wilhelm.Bessel.Ausschnitt.Daguerrotypie.png|thumb|upright|Crop of a [[Daguerreotype]] (1843)]]
While the observatory was still in construction Bessel elaborated the ''Fundamenta Astronomiae'' based on Bradley's observations. As a preliminary result he produced tables of [[atmospheric refraction]] that won him the [[Lalande Prize]] from the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 1811. The Königsberg Observatory began operation in 1813.

Starting in 1819, Bessel determined the position of over 50,000 stars with a [[meridian circle]] from [[Georg von Reichenbach|Reichenbach]], assisted by some of his qualified students. The most prominent of them was [[Friedrich Wilhelm Argelander]], his successors were [[Otto August Rosenberger]] and [[August Ludwig Busch]].

Bessel determined the first reliable value for the [[Cosmic distance ladder|distance]] between a star and the [[Solar System]] with a [[heliometer]] from [[Joseph von Fraunhofer|Fraunhofer]] using the method of [[stellar parallax]]. In 1838 he published a parallax of 0.314 [[arcsecond]]s for [[61 Cygni]], which indicated that the star is 10.3 [[Light-year|ly]] away.<ref>{{Cite journal | last = Bessel | first = F. W. | doi = 10.1002/asna.18390160502 | title = Bestimmung der Entfernung des 61sten Sterns des Schwans | language = de| trans-title = Determination of the distance to 61 Cygni| journal = Astronomische Nachrichten | volume = 16 | issue = 365–366 | pages = 65–96 | year = 1838 | bibcode = 1838AN.....16...65B| url = https://zenodo.org/record/1424605 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1093/mnras/4.17.152| last = Bessel | first = F. W. | title = On the parallax of 61 Cygni| journal = Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society| volume = 4| issue = 17| pages = 152–161| year = 1838b| bibcode = 1838MNRAS...4..152B| doi-access = free}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|title=A brief history of light dates|url=http://newswatch.nationalgeographic.com/2010/11/22/a_brief_history_of_light_years/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110415042634/http://newswatch.nationalgeographic.com/2010/11/22/a_brief_history_of_light_years/|archive-date=15 April 2011|magazine=National Geographic|access-date=26 June 2020}}</ref>  Compared with the current measurement of 11.4 ly, Bessel's figure had an error of 9.6%. Thanks to these results astronomers had not only enlarged the vision of the universe well beyond the cosmic magnitude, but after the discovery in 1728 by [[James Bradley]] of the [[Aberration (astronomy)|aberration of light]] a second empirical evidence of the Earth's relative movement was produced.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hamel |first=Jürgen |title=Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel |publisher=Teubner |location=Leipzig |year=1984 |page=69 }}</ref> A short time later [[Friedrich Georg Wilhelm Struve]] and [[Thomas James Henderson|Thomas Henderson]] reported the parallaxes of [[Vega]] and [[Alpha Centauri]].

Precise measurements with a new [[meridian circle]] from Adolf Repsold allowed Bessel to notice deviations in the motions of [[Sirius]] and [[Procyon]], which must be caused by the gravitational attraction of unseen companions.<ref>
{{Cite journal | last = Bessel | first = F. W. | title = Ueber Veränderlichkeit der eigenen Bewegungen der Fixsterne | language = de| trans-title = On Variations of the proper motions of the fixed stars| doi = 10.1002/asna.18450221002 | journal = Astronomische Nachrichten | volume = 22 | issue = 514, 515| pages = 145–160, 169–184 | year = 1844a| bibcode = 1844AN.....22..145B| url = https://zenodo.org/record/1424611 }}
</ref><ref>
{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1093/mnras/6.11.136a| last = Bessel | first = F. W. | title = On the variations of the proper motions of Procyon and Sirius| journal = Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society| volume = 6| issue = 11| pages = 136–141| year = 1844c| bibcode = 1844MNRAS...6R.136B| doi-access = free}}
</ref>
His announcement of Sirius's "dark companion" in 1844 was the first correct claim of a previously unobserved companion by positional measurement, and eventually led to the discovery of [[Sirius B]] by [[Alvan Graham Clark]] in 1862, the first discovery of a [[white dwarf]]. [[John Martin Schaeberle]] discovered Procyon B in 1896.

Bessel was the first scientist who realized the effect later called ''[[personal equation]]'', that several simultaneously observing persons determine slightly different values, especially recording the transit time of stars.<ref>
{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1017/s0007087407009478| last = Hoffmann | first = Christoph | title = Constant differences: Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel, the concept of the observer in early nineteenth-century practical astronomy and the history of the personal equation| journal = British Journal for the History of Science| volume = 40| issue = 3| pages = 333–365| year = 2007| s2cid = 170080943 }}
</ref>

In 1824, Bessel developed a new method for calculating the circumstances of eclipses using the so-called [[Besselian elements]].  His method simplified the calculation to such an extent, without sacrificing accuracy, that it is still in use.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEcat5/beselm.html | title = Besselian Elements of Solar Eclipses | last = [[Fred Espenak|Espenak]] | first = Fred | website = NASA Eclipse Website | access-date = 4 August 2023}}</ref>

On Bessel's proposal the [[Prussian Academy of Sciences]] started the edition of the ''Berliner Akademische Sternkarten'' (''Berlin Academic Star Charts'')  in 1825 as an international project with [[Johann Franz Encke]] as executive editor. One unpublished new chart enabled [[Johann Gottfried Galle]] to find [[discovery of Neptune|Neptune]] near the position calculated by [[Urbain Le Verrier|Le Verrier]] in September 1846 at [[Berlin Observatory]].

In the 18th century a series of cylinder functions were introduced to solve [[string vibration]] problems by [[Daniel Bernoulli]], [[Leonhard Euler]] and others. These functions were used by [[Joseph-Louis Lagrange]] and Bessel to solve the [[Kepler's equation]]. Bessel later systematically studied the mathematical properties of these functions, now known as [[Bessel function]]s.<ref name=":0" /> These functions are critical for the solution of certain [[differential equations]], these functions are used throughout both classical and [[quantum physics]]. In his studies of this functions, Bessel published for the first time the [[Fourier series]], before [[Joseph Fourier]] who had worked on it but his work was published decades later.<ref name=":0" />

A [[Bessel's correction|correction]] term in the formula for the [[sample variance]] estimator is named in his honour. This is the use of the factor ''n''&nbsp;−&nbsp;1 in the denominator of the formula, rather than just ''n''. This occurs when the ''sample mean'' rather than the ''population mean'' is used to centre the data and since the sample mean is a linear combination of the data the residual to the sample mean overcounts the number of degrees of freedom by the number of constraint equations — in this case one.

[[File:Igm, apparato di bessel, del 1873.jpg|thumb|Bessel's geodetic apparatus, in the museum of Istituto Geografico Militare, Florence, Italy]]
Like numerous astronomers of his time Bessel dealt on the field of [[geodesy]], too,<ref>{{cite conference
|first = T.
|last = Viik
|title = F.W. Bessel and Geodesy
|date = 2006
|conference = Struve Geodetic Arc 2006 International Conference: The Struve Arc and Extensions in Space and Time. 13–15 August 2006
|location = Haparanda and Pajala, Sweden
|publisher = Lantmäteriet, Gävle, Sweden, 2006
|pages = 53–63
|url = http://www.aai.ee/~viik/PAPERS/BESSEL_GEODESY.pdf
|access-date = 9 November 2013
|archive-date = 9 November 2013
|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131109130501/http://www.aai.ee/~viik/PAPERS/BESSEL_GEODESY.pdf
}}</ref>
first theoretically, when he published a method for solving the main [[Geodesics on an ellipsoid|geodetic problem]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last = Bessel | first = F. W. | title = Ueber die Berechnungen der geographischen Länge und Breite aus geodätischen Vermessungen | language = de | doi = 10.1002/asna.18260041601| journal = Astronomische Nachrichten | volume = 4 | issue = 16| pages = 241–254 | year = 1825 | arxiv = 0908.1823 | bibcode = | s2cid = 118630614 | url =  }}
* {{Cite journal | last = Bessel | first = F. W. | translator-last = Ch. F. Karney  |  translator-first = R. E. Deakin | title = The calculation of longitude and latitude from geodesic measurements | language = en | doi = 10.1002/asna.201011352| journal = Astronomische Nachrichten | volume = 333 | issue = 8| pages = 852–861 | year = 2010 | arxiv = 0908.1824 | bibcode = 2010AN....331..852K | s2cid = 118760590 | url =  }} [https://geographiclib.sourceforge.net/bessel-errata.html Errata].</ref>
In 1830 he got the royal order for the survey of [[East Prussia]] with the purpose to connect the yet existing Prussian and Russian [[triangulation network]]s. This work was carried out in cooperation with [[Johann Jacob Baeyer]], then major of the Prussian army; the final report was published in 1838.<ref>{{cite book | first1 = F. W. | last1 = Bessel| author-link1 = Friedrich Bessel | first2 = J. J. | last2 = Baeyer | title = Gradmessung in Ostpreussen und ihre Verbindung mit Preussischen und Russischen Dreiecksketten | language = de| trans-title = The East Prussian Survey and its connection with the Prussian and Russian networks | publisher = Dümmler | location = Berlin | date = 1838 | url = https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_f5AAAAAAMAAJ}}</ref>
He also obtained an estimate of increased accuracy for the [[Earth's ellipsoid]], nowadays called the [[Bessel ellipsoid]], based on several [[arc measurements]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last = Bessel | first = F. W. | doi = 10.1002/asna.18370142301 | title = Bestimmung der Axen des elliptischen Rotationssphäroids, welches den vorhandenen Messungen von Meridianbögen der Erde am meisten entspricht | language = de| trans-title = Determination of the axes of ellipsoid that fits best to the existing measurements of meridian arcs| journal = Astronomische Nachrichten | volume = 14 | issue = 333 | pages = 333–346| year = 1837 | bibcode = 1837AN.....14..333B | url = https://zenodo.org/record/1424603 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last = Bessel | first = F. W. | doi = 10.1002/asna.18420190702 | title = Ueber einen Fehler in der Berechnung der französischen Gradmessung und seinen Einfluß auf die Bestimmung der Figur der Erde | language = de| trans-title = Concerning an error in the calculation of the French survey and its influence on the determination of the figure of the Earth| journal = Astronomische Nachrichten | volume = 19 | issue = 438| pages = 97–116| year = 1841 | bibcode = 1841AN.....19...97B| url = https://zenodo.org/record/1424607 }}</ref>

== Honors and prizes ==
* Honorary doctor degree from the [[University of Göttingen]] in March 1811
* [[Lalande Prize]] of the French Academy of Sciences in 1811 and 1816<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=biIgAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA460 M. E. Maidron : Le Prix d#Astronomie fondé par Lalande], p. 460, 461</ref>
* Member of the [[Prussian Academy of Sciences]] in 1812<ref>{{cite web | title = Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel | url = https://www.bbaw.de/die-akademie/akademie-historische-aspekte/mitglieder-historisch/historisches-mitglied-friedrich-wilhelm-bessel-200 | publisher = Berlin-Brandenburgische Akademie der Wissenschaften | access-date = 23 April 2023}}</ref>
* Member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 1816<ref>{{cite web | title = Les membres du passé | url = https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-depuis-la-creation-de-l-Academie-des-sciences/les-membres-du-passe-dont-le-nom-commence-par-b.html | publisher = Académie des Sciences – Institut de France | access-date = 23 April 2023}}</ref>
* Foreign member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 1823
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1825<ref>{{cite web | title = Fellows | url = https://catalogues.royalsociety.org/CalmView/Overview.aspx?src=CalmView.Persons&r=(((Surname=%27Bessel%27))) | publisher = The Royal Society | access-date = 23 April 2023}}</ref>
* Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1832<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter B|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060618085806/http://amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf |archive-date=2006-06-18 |url-status=live|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=24 June 2011}}</ref>
* Member of the Royal Institute of the Netherlands, predecessor of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1827<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dwc.knaw.nl/biografie/pmknaw/?pagetype=authorDetail&aId=PE00002153 |title=Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel (1784–1846) |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |access-date=22 May 2016}}</ref>
* Member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 1840<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?year=1840;year-max=1840;smode=advanced;startDoc=21|access-date=9 April 2021|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>
* Member of the [[Accademia nazionale delle scienze|National Academy of Science]] in Verona (1842),<ref>{{cite web | title = Elenco Cronologico soci stranieri | url = https://www.accademiaxl.it/accademia/elenco-cronologico-soci-stranieri/ | publisher = Accademia nazionale delle scienze | access-date = 12 April 2024}}</ref>
* Bessel won the [[Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society]] twice, in 1829 and 1841<ref>{{Cite web | title = The Gold Medal | url = https://ras.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2021-03/Gold%20Medal%202021.pdf | access-date = 23 April 2023 | website = Royal Astronomical Society}}</ref>

Bessel was one of the first members of the [[Order Pour le Merite#Civil class|Order Pour le Merite]] (Civil class) when it was established in 1842.<ref>{{cite web | title = Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel | url = https://www.orden-pourlemerite.de/mitglieder/franz-friedrich-wilhelm-bessel?m=2&u=1&p=2 | publisher = Orden pour le Mérite für Wissenschaften und Künste | access-date = 23 April 2023}}</ref>

The first cosmic object named after Bessel is [[Bessel (crater)|the largest crater]] in the Moon's [[Mare Serenitatis]].<ref>Wilhelm Beer, Johann Heinrich Mädler: Der Mond nach seinen kosmischen und individuellen Verhältnissen oder allgemeine vergleichende Selenographie. Berlin 1837, S. 231–232</ref> The [[main-belt]] asteroid [[1552&nbsp;Bessel]] was named at the centenary of the parallax determination in 1938.<ref name="1552-Bessel" />

Geographical commemorations are two fjords in Greenland, [[Bessel Fjord|Bessel Fjord, NE Greenland]] and [[Bessel Fjord, NW Greenland]].

''Xyletinus besseli''<ref>{{Cite journal | title = Xyletinus besseli Alekseev & Bukejs 2019, sp.nov | journal = Zenodo | date = 2019 | url = https://zenodo.org/records/5945261 | language=en | doi = 10.5281/zenodo.5945261 | last1 = Alekseev | first1 = Vitalii I. | last2 = Bukejs | first2 = Andris }}</ref> a fossil [[beetle]] from the [[Eocene]] belonging to the family [[Ptinidae]], found in the [[Baltic amber]] in [[Sambia Peninsula|Sambia]], was named in his honour.<ref name="Alekseev Bukejs 2019 p. ">{{cite journal | last1=Alekseev | first1=Vitalii I. | last2=Bukejs | first2=Andris | title=Two new species of Xyletinus Latreille (Ptinidae: Xyletininae) in Eocene Baltic amber | journal=Zootaxa | volume=4668 | issue=4 | date=2019-09-12 |issn=1175-5334 | doi=10.11646/zootaxa.4668.4.5 | pmid=31716608 | s2cid=203411805 | url=https://www.checklistbank.org/dataset/25466 }}</ref>

BeSSel, the [https://www3.mpifr-bonn.mpg.de/staff/abrunthaler/BeSSeL/index.shtml ''Bar and Spiral Structure Legacy Survey''], is named after him.
